entradas.text: The sun was starting to peek through the blinds of my suite in The Grand Chariot Hotel in Anrica.
I hadn't slept at all that night. I was too busy thinking about how I would rally my party's conservative base at today's election kickoff.
I was just pulling on my clothes when two soft, sharp knocks came at the door. Lucian.
"Good morning, sir."
"Now what?"
entradas.menu: "Now what?"

entradas.text: "Morning, Lucian."
entradas.menu: "Morning, Lucian."

entradas.text: "I hope you brought coffee."
entradas.menu: "I hope you brought coffee."

entradas.text: Lucian unclasped his briefcase and took out a small, disc-shaped device. After scanning the room with it, he gave a satisfied nod.
"I've just received the final results of your investigation into the Old Guard."
"It's about your investigation into the Oligarchs."
"I've just received an update regarding the investigation you ordered into the opposition:"
"Great. What'd they dig up on the PFJP?"
entradas.menu: "Great. What'd they dig up on the PFJP?"

entradas.text: "Great. What'd they dig up on the NFP?"
entradas.menu: "Great. What'd they dig up on the NFP?"

entradas.text: "It had better be juicy after this long."
entradas.menu: "It had better be juicy after this long."

entradas.text: "It had better be juicy after this long."
entradas.menu: "It had better be juicy after this long."

entradas.text: Lucian left the room. I finished putting on my tie and reread my notes for the morning's speech.
Lucian pulled out a folder and opened it.
"I told you, Lucian, you're vice president now. You don't need to keep calling me 'sir'."
entradas.menu: "I told you, Lucian, you're vice president now. Stop calling me 'sir'."

entradas.text: "Force of habit, si-- Anton."
"About goddamn time."
entradas.menu: "About goddamn time."

entradas.text: "Well? Don't leave me in suspense."
entradas.menu: "Well? Don't leave me in suspense."

entradas.text: "What's left of them, you mean."
entradas.menu: "What's left of them, you mean."

entradas.text: "Trust me, there's more to the Old Guard than Hawker and the Supreme Court."
Lucian pulled out a folder and opened it.
"I have some more news. About the PFJP."
"Now that that's settled, I'll let you prepare for your rally."
"Now that that's settled, I'll let you prepare for your rally."
"I have some more news. About the NFP."
"Before I begin, I have to ask if you're sure you wish to follow through on this investigation. After all, Tusk has been an ally throughout your term."
"I don't care. Give me the dirt on Tusk."
entradas.menu: "I don't care. Give me the dirt on Tusk."

entradas.text: "Good point. Maybe I don't need to hear the results."
entradas.menu: "Good point. Maybe I don't need to hear the results."

entradas.text: "Now that that's settled, I'll let you prepare for your rally."
"Now that that's settled, I'll let you prepare for your rally."
Lucian sat down in the suite's office chair and pulled a piece of paper from his jacket pocket.
"I just thought I'd drop off some talking points for your speech today."
"That's not even your job anymore."
entradas.menu: "That's not even your job anymore."

entradas.text: "Don't worry. I won't say anything stupid."
entradas.menu: "Don't worry. I won't say anything stupid."

entradas.text: "Just like old times."
entradas.menu: "Just like old times."

entradas.text: "Indeed. Four long years ago."
"I never said you would."
"My job is to support you. Just like always."
"Much appreciated."
entradas.menu: "Much appreciated."

entradas.text: "No trouble at all."
"Ready to hit the campaign trail again?"
entradas.menu: "Ready to hit the campaign trail again?"

entradas.text: "Are you sure you can take another four more years of me?"
entradas.menu: "Are you sure you can take another four more years of me?"

entradas.text: "I've got to finish getting ready."
entradas.menu: "I've got to finish getting ready."

entradas.text: Lucian smiled tightly, but didn't answer the question.
"I'm ready if you are, Mr. President."
"Of course."
"I'll see you at the rally."
A few hours later, I was waiting in the wings at the Norsord Auditorium in Anrica. In the audience were several thousand of my conservative supporters.
"Victory Is Close."
"Peace, Prosperity, and the Sordish Way."
"Your Land. My Land. Sordland."
"I almost forgot. The Archpriest of Deyr couldn't be present today, but wanted to relay a message of support to you and your family."
"'I bless the Raynes down in Anrica.'"
"I don't want his support."

entradas.text: "Very well, sir."
Anrica Mayor Curtan Leste made a few brief introductory comments. I couldn't look at him without thinking about how I'd let Monica down.
Everyone cheered as I walked onstage -- except for a scowling Mayor Curtan Leste. He had tried to escape my shadow by joining the NFP, only to be defeated once more when our parties became allies.
